newsitem.title: USA: Aames seen as takeover target- Business Week.
newsitem.headline: Aames seen as takeover target- Business Week.

text.p: Aames Financial Corp is seen as a possible takeover target, according to Business Week, which cited an unnamed money manager.
According to the magazine, the money manager believes an "acquisition-hungry franchiser and financing company is hot on the trail of Aames."

Aames, which provides home-equity loans in 23 states, has also attracted the attention of bargain hunting investors, including the Fesbash brothers, best known for their short-selling in the 1980s, the magazine said.
Now, the brothers are bullish on Aames stock, with or without a takeover, Business Week said.
That's because Aames shares have fallen to 13-5/8 as of Thursday's close from about 32 in mid-March, partly because the company disappointed some analysts on earnings.
The stock has a takeover value of about 25, the magazine estimated.
Aames officials were not immediately available to comment. The company is based in Los Angeles.
